clue.text: A tree providing cane

definitions.meaning: a slender broadleaf tree with pale, papery bark
as a verb, to cane is to beat with a rod as a school punishment

explanation.surface: A tree supplies the wood from which a walking stick is cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'providing' just links the two senses; the second is the old school punishment of beating with a bundle of twigs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the silver-barked tree and the act of flogging with its twigs, a synonym for caning.

clue.text: Inexpert dive caused by sagging paunch

parts.note: a paunch is a pot belly
to flop is to sag or hang down limply

explanation.surface: A clumsy dive is blamed on the diver's drooping gut.
explanation.definitionFit: A clumsy plunge where the swimmer lands flat on the stomach with a painful slap.

clue.text: Fierce enough to make sheep gasp

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
to pant is to gasp for breath

explanation.surface: Something so savage it leaves a sheep breathless.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrestrained and violent, as a lion reared up on a heraldic shield, so a synonym for wild and ferocious.

clue.text: Barbarian king was a big, handsome man

parts.note: the Huns were barbarian invaders of the Roman Empire
K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: A tribal warlord of old turns out to have been a looker.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for a well-built, attractive male.

clue.text: Superior sixth formers

definitions.meaning: pupils in the top two years of a British secondary school, the highest year group

explanation.surface: Older pupils at school think themselves a cut above the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The sixth form is the top level of a British secondary school, so its pupils are, playfully, the uppermost form.
explanation.definitionFit: Means excellent or upmarket, and punningly describes pupils in the uppermost year group.

clue.text: Travel by tube to escape detection

definitions.meaning: the Tube is London's underground railway, so to ride it is to journey below the streets
to go into hiding, as a resistance fighter or fugitive does

explanation.surface: Someone takes the Tube to shake off a pursuer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the London Underground railway; 'to' is the link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a trip on the subway railway, and idiomatically going into hiding from the authorities.

clue.text: Many query whether it contains liquor

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
to query is to ask

explanation.surface: Lots of people wonder whether there is drink inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden barrel in which wine, beer or spirits are stored.

clue.text: In conflict with Muslim leader this month

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish or Muslim military commander or chief
inst. (instant) is an old business abbreviation for this month

explanation.surface: Opposing a Muslim chief during the present month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inst.' is old commercial shorthand, as in 'your letter of the 5th inst.', meaning this month.
explanation.definitionFit: A preposition meaning opposed to or at odds with something.

clue.text: Resolved to raise money

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means writing it from the bottom up

parts.note: banknotes are paper money

explanation.surface: Someone is determined to raise funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to raise' turns the word for paper money upside down in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Being determined on something, as in having one's heart fixed on a plan.

clue.text: Moans from limping pole upset pious man

parts.note: lame means limping
N is the north pole

indicators.note: upset tips the abbreviation over so it reads backwards

parts.note: a pious man is a saint, abbreviated ST

explanation.surface: Groans come from a hobbling pole-vaulter whom a holy man knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the saint's abbreviation round; 'from' just links the definition to the wordplay, and the pole is a compass point, not a vaulting pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Laments are expressions of grief or complaints, synonyms for wails and groans.

clue.text: Patrick Moore?

parts.note: the astronomer who presented The Sky at Night on British television for decades: a celebrated performer, and one who talked about heavenly bodies

explanation.surface: A question naming a famous British TV astronomer.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Patrick Moore presented the BBC astronomy programme The Sky at Night for over fifty years, so he was a television entertainer whose subject was the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading entertainer, and punningly an astronomer whose act was about the night sky.

clue.text: He's certainly not of elevated origin!

definitions.text: He's certainly not of elevated origin!

parts.words: He's certainly not of elevated origin!
parts.note: a person who has risen from humble beginnings, though read word by word the term suggests a lofty beginning

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a man of lowly birth.
explanation.walkthrough: Split, the word suggests a raised beginning, which is the opposite of what it means: someone newly risen who has acquired status above their roots.
explanation.definitionFit: A pushy person who has suddenly risen in rank and acts above their humble background.

clue.text: Some very early flowers bloom for months

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few early-season plants flower for many months.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the join of 'very' and 'early'.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar span of twelve months, across which flowers come and go.

clue.text: Musical group accompanies a former African leader

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: A band plays along with an ex-president from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Hastings Banda was the first president of Malawi, ruling from 1964 to 1994.
explanation.definitionFit: Hastings Kamuzu Banda, Malawi's first president and long-time ruler.

clue.text: Article about to appear shortly

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece on a subject will be published soon.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for soon, in a little while.

clue.text: Rex leaves quickly to make sauce

indicators.note: leaves means the letter goes away from the word

parts.note: presto is the musical direction for a quick tempo
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: The king rushes off to whip up a sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' removes R (Rex, king, as in the royal cipher) from PRESTO.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian basil-and-pine-nut paste served with pasta.

clue.text: Essentially bluish-grey

definitions.meaning: an old word for a dark greyish-blue colour

explanation.surface: A colour description: basically a sort of slate.
explanation.walkthrough: Perse is an archaic colour name for a dark blue-grey; the Latin phrase means 'by itself'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means intrinsically, and run together it is an old colour term for slaty blue.

clue.text: Landlord with complete mastery of his lines

definitions.note: the definition is a noun phrase while the answer is an adjective: having complete mastery of one's lines

parts.note: a landlord lets property, so is a letter
perfect means complete, entire

explanation.surface: A landlord who is also an actor knows his script cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with complete' does double duty in the surface: 'complete' gives PERFECT, and the answer describes an actor who has total command of the script.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes an actor who knows the script word for word, without a single slip.

clue.text: Flier given wartime rations

definitions.meaning: a large thrush that winters in Britain
food served to soldiers in the field, on campaign

explanation.surface: A pilot is handed wartime food allowances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' links the two readings: the bird, and food eaten by troops in the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A migratory thrush, and split up, the food soldiers eat on campaign.

clue.text: Ideal place to purchase wild-life book?

definitions.text: Ideal place to purchase wild-life book?

parts.words: Ideal place to purchase wild-life book?
parts.note: read literally, the phrase means booking a natural-history title in advance, but it is a protected area for animals and plants

explanation.surface: Where would you best buy a natural history book?
explanation.walkthrough: To reserve a book is to order it in advance, so the phrase seems to be about booking a title on the natural world.
explanation.definitionFit: A protected area where wildlife and habitats are conserved.

clue.text: Token taken from northern oilman in error

indicators.note: in error says the letters of oilman are set down wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A small gesture is extracted from a northern oil worker by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in error' rearranges OILMAN into OMINAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Token in the sense of a small, symbolic amount, as a token payment.

clue.text: Top people appear in right clothing

indicators.note: in places the top people inside the abbreviation for right

parts.note: A1 means first-class, top, with the 1 read as I
men means people

explanation.surface: The elite show up in correct dress.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means first-rate, and setters often read its digit 1 as the letter I. 'appear' is a link; 'in' sets the top people inside the abbreviation for right.
explanation.definitionFit: An old literary word for garments or dress.

clue.text: Hesitate to take off sweater in spring

indicators.note: taking off means removing the hesitation sound from the end of the garment

parts.note: a jumper is a sweater, the British word
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone dithers about removing a pullover once the weather warms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take off' removes ER, the sound of hesitation, from JUMPER, the British word for a sweater. 'Spring' wants to be the season; it is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To leap or bound into the air.

clue.text: He can judge a horse

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

explanation.surface: A man able to assess a horse's quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' stands for a man's name, here the biblical patriarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name, borne by the Old Testament patriarch, so it can stand for a male person.

clue.text: Dress elaborately to bring dog back

indicators.note: back says the dog's name is read in the other direction

parts.note: a pug is a small snub-nosed dog

explanation.surface: Getting dressed up in order to fetch the dog home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the dog's name round, and it follows 'to' taken as written; 'bring' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on smart or fancy clothes, an informal phrasal verb.

clue.text: Jam needs to gel

definitions.meaning: a tight spot or predicament, a fix
to stick together or set firm

explanation.surface: Kitchen advice: preserves must set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs to' links the two senses; 'Jam' is the predicament, not the preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Means an awkward predicament, and also to cohere or stick together.

clue.text: Pre-eminent Indian leader in top gear

parts.note: top means best, pre-eminent

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word Indian

explanation.surface: A leading Indian politician is in the best equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top gear' is clothing for the head, not the fastest gear of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A topi is a lightweight sun helmet worn in India, so it is headwear.

clue.text: Disgusting breach of sporting etiquette

definitions.meaning: an illegal or unfair act in a game

explanation.surface: Calling out bad sportsmanship as revolting.
explanation.definitionFit: Means repulsive, and also an infringement of the rules in sport.

clue.text: Fit in with study group

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study
a form is a school class, a group of pupils

explanation.surface: Joining in with a tutorial group to fit in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'con' is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart; a form is a class in a British school.
explanation.definitionFit: To comply with rules or social norms, matching the crowd.

clue.text: Physician holds one plant in front of a second one

indicators.note: in front of places the flower-filled piece before the letter A
the physician's abbreviation holds the flower inside it

parts.note: DR is short for doctor, a physician
a rose is one kind of plant

explanation.surface: A doctor holds one plant ahead of another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second one' is the definition: another plant, the sundew. 'holds' puts the flower inside the doctor's title, and 'in front of' places that before A.
explanation.definitionFit: Drosera is the genus of sundews, carnivorous bog plants, so it is another plant.

clue.text: Said brill should be served out before game

indicators.note: served out suggests the letters dished up in a new arrangement, like fish portioned on a plate

explanation.surface: Brill, it is said, must be dished up before the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served out' rearranges SAIDBRILL; brill is a flatfish, which makes 'served' look culinary.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue sport played on a cloth-covered table with three balls.

clue.text: Fired by fellow of flexible frame

parts.note: lit means set alight, fired
he stands for a man, a fellow

explanation.surface: A supple man is set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Supple and agile in body, a synonym for limber.
